included_members.abstraction: Phase-change recovery and purification loop: Condense and separate contaminants from the solvent, then purify and return the solvent to service, maintaining solvent quality and minimizing consumption.
included_members.label: Phase-change recovery and purification loop
included_members.description: Condense and separate contaminants from the solvent, then purify and return the solvent to service, maintaining solvent quality and minimizing consumption.
included_members.explanation: Condenses/purifies and recycles the solvent—closed-loop management within a non-aqueous solvent system.

included_members.idea_text: After a very brief, minimal-water pre-treatment or stain removal, garments are placed in a sealed chamber. Any residual water is replaced with liquid CO2 (or another suitable transitional fluid). The system then takes the CO2 past its critical point, transforming it into a gas. This allows for extremely gentle, residue-free drying without surface tension effects, preventing shrinkage or distortion, and contributing to overall lower water usage by enabling minimal wetting initially.
included_members.abstraction: Displace residual water with a transitional fluid and remove moisture via phase change: Introduce a non-aqueous or transitional fluid to replace remaining water in textiles, then induce a controlled phase transition (e.g., liquid → supercritical/gas) of that fluid to effect drying and residue-free removal of moisture while avoiding capillary/surface-tension damage.
included_members.label: Displace residual water with a transitional fluid and remove moisture via phase change
included_members.description: Introduce a non-aqueous or transitional fluid to replace remaining water in textiles, then induce a controlled phase transition (e.g., liquid → supercritical/gas) of that fluid to effect drying and residue-free removal of moisture while avoiding capillary/surface-tension damage.
included_members.explanation: Replaces water with a transitional non-aqueous fluid and removes it via phase change (e.g., supercritical/gas), matching non-aqueous/phase-change media.

included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning system where clothes are briefly exposed to a very fine mist of a fabric-safe, non-toxic, supersaturated crystalline salt solution. Cycles of controlled humidity reduction and re-humidification are then applied in a dry chamber. As the salt crystals grow within the fabric pores and around dirt particles, they exert micro-mechanical stresses. When humidity changes, they re-crystallize or shrink, causing embedded dirt to physically detach from the fibers. The loosened dirt and salt residue are then removed by a gentle vacuum and filtration system, achieving cleaning with minimal water and no harsh chemicals.
included_members.abstraction: Crystallization-driven micro-mechanical extraction: Induce crystal nucleation and growth inside fiber pores and around soils so that crystal growth and dissolution apply micro-scale mechanical forces to detach contaminants.
included_members.label: Crystallization-driven micro-mechanical extraction
included_members.description: Induce crystal nucleation and growth inside fiber pores and around soils so that crystal growth and dissolution apply micro-scale mechanical forces to detach contaminants.
included_members.explanation: Relies on induced crystallization/solidification and dissolution (phase-change medium) to generate cleaning forces.

included_members.idea_text: A closed-loop, high-pressure cleaning chamber that exposes garments to a minimal amount of near-critical water (e.g., 250-350 °C, 5-15 MPa). In this state, water effectively dissolves and cleanses organic dirt, oils, and greases from fabric fibers without harsh detergents. After a short cycle, the system rapidly cools and depressurizes the water, causing contaminants to precipitate out for easy filtration and removal. The purified water is then recycled, achieving powerful cleaning with dramatically reduced water consumption and no chemical discharge.
included_members.abstraction: Near‑critical/high‑temperature, high‑pressure water solvent cleaning: Operate water at elevated temperature and pressure near its critical region so its solvent power and transport characteristics remove organic soils and oils from fabric fibers without added detergents.
included_members.label: Near‑critical/high‑temperature, high‑pressure water solvent cleaning
included_members.description: Operate water at elevated temperature and pressure near its critical region so its solvent power and transport characteristics remove organic soils and oils from fabric fibers without added detergents.
included_members.explanation: Cleans using water in an altered high-T/high-P near-critical state—leveraging phase/state behavior as the cleaning medium.

included_members.idea_text: A closed-loop, high-pressure cleaning chamber that exposes garments to a minimal amount of near-critical water (e.g., 250-350 °C, 5-15 MPa). In this state, water effectively dissolves and cleanses organic dirt, oils, and greases from fabric fibers without harsh detergents. After a short cycle, the system rapidly cools and depressurizes the water, causing contaminants to precipitate out for easy filtration and removal. The purified water is then recycled, achieving powerful cleaning with dramatically reduced water consumption and no chemical discharge.
included_members.abstraction: Rapid quench/depressurization to precipitate contaminants: After solvent-stage cleaning, rapidly cool and/or depressurize the fluid to force dissolved contaminants out of solution or into a separable phase for collection.
included_members.label: Rapid quench/depressurization to precipitate contaminants
included_members.description: After solvent-stage cleaning, rapidly cool and/or depressurize the fluid to force dissolved contaminants out of solution or into a separable phase for collection.
included_members.explanation: Uses rapid depressurization/quench to force phase separation/precipitation of dissolved soils—state/phase-change separation.

nodes.name: Minimal-water localized wet cleaning (films, mist, foam, bubbles)
nodes.description: Use thin films/mists/foams/bubbles plus local agitation or chemistry to clean with tiny liquid volumes.
idea_text: A targeted spray or applicator pen that dispenses a concentrated blend of fabric-safe enzymes onto specific stains. After a short dwell time, the broken-down stain components can be wiped away with a damp cloth or absorbed by a dry, absorbent pad, eliminating the need for a full water wash for localized soiling.

A washing device designed with micro-channels or textured surfaces where clothes are exposed to a very thin film of water or cleaning solution. Transducers generate targeted acoustic streaming within this film, creating microscopic "scrubbing" action that cleans fabric at a surface level with significantly reduced water volume compared to traditional methods.

A controlled environment cabinet or low-humidity wash chamber that introduces a fine mist containing beneficial, fabric-safe microbes. These microbes, under optimal conditions of temperature and humidity, "consume" odor-causing compounds and light organic soiling on garments, effectively cleaning them over a gentle, longer cycle with minimal water input.

Design a cleaning chamber where clothes are gently suspended in a minimal volume of water or a specialized, low-surface-tension cleaning solution. A system of diffusers beneath the garments introduces precisely controlled, pulsed streams of fine air or inert gas bubbles. These bubbles percolate through the fabric, creating a gentle "scrubbing" action that dislodges dirt and impurities, which are then collected from the circulating minimal liquid.

Develop cleaning agents or fabric coatings containing embedded or surface-applied smart polymers. When triggered (e.g., by a slight temperature change or pH adjustment in a low-humidity chamber with minimal mist), these polymers swell, physically pushing dirt and grime out of the fabric pores. Upon a reverse trigger, they contract, squeezing out any trapped impurities or dirty water, which is then collected, significantly reducing water usage for cleaning and rinsing.

A washing device featuring a textured internal surface or specialized micro-channels. Garments are laid flat or gently rolled across this surface while a very thin, continuously flowing film of water or cleaning solution is introduced. The micro-scale geometry of the surface generates localized fluid shear forces that effectively "peel" and dislodge surface dirt and oils from the fabric with an extremely low volume of liquid, which is then filtered and recirculated.

Design a washing machine drum where clothes are exposed to a minimal amount of water (or a specialized cleaning solution), which is then agitated by powerful ultrasonic transducers. This intense cavitation provides deep cleaning with significantly less water and mechanical friction than traditional methods.

A system where garments are briefly immersed in a minimal volume of a low-viscosity, fabric-safe MR fluid. A pulsed magnetic field is then applied, causing the fluid to momentarily thicken around the fabric fibers, effectively encapsulating and mechanically stressing embedded dirt and oil particles. When the field is removed, the fluid instantly thins, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then carried away by filtration. The fluid is continuously recycled and purified for subsequent uses with minimal loss and no water.

A specialized, highly reusable sheet or pad made from a superhydrophilic, finely textured material designed to be placed in a tumbling dryer or a dedicated refresh cabinet with clothes. During a brief cycle with a very fine, minimal mist of water, this sheet actively attracts and captures body oils, dissolved dirt, and fine particulate matter released from the garments. The superhydrophilic material "wicks" and holds these contaminants, effectively cleaning the clothes with minimal water, and the sheet is then rinsed clean for reuse.

A sealed laundry cabinet that cleans and refreshes clothes using a fine mist of water combined with eco-friendly cleaning agents. The mist humidifies and helps release dirt particles, which are then condensed, collected, and filtered, effectively cleaning with very low water usage per cycle.

Garments are exposed to a minimal, fine mist of water and a cleaning agent, just enough to lightly wet the fabric and encapsulate dirt. The wetted garment is then gently frozen (e.g., with chilled air) and placed in a low-pressure chamber. The frozen cleaning solution and dirt sublimate away, removing contaminants directly from the fabric structure without liquid drainage or mechanical stress, resulting in clean, dry clothes with minimal water usage.

Garments are manufactured with embedded, fabric-safe microcapsules containing a concentrated, low-water cleaning agent or odor neutralizer. When the garment is worn or experiences mild mechanical stress (e.g., gentle tumbling in a refresh cabinet with slight humidity), some capsules burst, releasing their contents to spot-clean, remove odors, or refresh the fabric locally, significantly extending the time between full water washes.

A flat or slightly curved surface where garments are laid. A system of precise nozzles applies micro-droplets of a specialized, low-surface-tension cleaning solution to stained areas. Electrodes beneath the surface then apply electric fields to dynamically move, oscillate, or "scrub" these droplets over the fabric, dislodging dirt. The dirty droplets are then electro-wetting-guided to a collection port, allowing for extremely targeted cleaning with minuscule water usage.

A targeted handheld device or a small chamber with specialized electrodes. Garments, or specific soiled areas, are exposed to a minimal film of a slightly conductive, fabric-safe electrolyte solution. An electric current is then precisely applied, generating reactive species or directly oxidizing organic dirt, stains, and odor molecules on the fabric surface. These contaminants are electrochemically degraded into simpler, water-soluble, or volatile compounds, which are then wiped away or evaporated, minimizing water usage and avoiding harsh chemicals.

A low-water washing system that uses a mild, biodegradable solution containing engineered humic acid analogues or naturally derived humic substances. These compounds act as powerful chelating and dispersing agents, effectively binding to dirt, oils, and metal ions embedded in fabric. This complexation process makes the contaminants easier to rinse away with a minimal amount of water, which is then purified and recycled through a system optimized to separate the humic-dirt complexes.

A targeted spray or minimal-water immersion system utilizing specific, non-toxic, fabric-safe plant-derived phytochemicals that are known to solubilize or emulsify fatty/waxy substances, similar to how plant cuticles are degraded. These agents would weaken the adhesion of oily dirt and grime to fabric fibers, allowing for easy removal with minimal water rinsing or wiping, without relying on broad-spectrum enzymes or microbes.

A precision stain removal device that generates and applies microscopic, targeted droplets of a highly concentrated, fabric-safe cleaning agent. Each droplet is designed to penetrate and then encapsulate a specific dirt particle or stain molecule. After a short dwell time, a mild vacuum or absorbent pad removes these dirt-encapsulating droplets, providing highly localized and efficient stain removal with minimal liquid use, preventing spreading and eliminating the need for a full wash.

Garments are woven with a percentage of specialized, micro-scale stimuli-responsive fibers (e.g., pH or humidity-sensitive polymers). When the garment is exposed to a minimal, fine mist of water with a specific pH, these embedded fibers swell, physically pushing outwards and dislodging dirt particles from the fabric structure. A subsequent change (e.g., mild heating or pH neutralization) causes the fibers to shrink, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration system, achieving cleaning with very low water input.

A low-water washing system that utilizes a highly concentrated, yet gentle, biodegradable biosurfactant foam. Garments are placed in a chamber where a precise, minimal amount of water, cleaning agents, and biosurfactant is agitated to create a dense, stable foam. Clothes are gently tumbled through this foam, allowing the biosurfactants to lift and emulsify dirt with minimal bulk water. The foam is then collapsed, and the concentrated dirty liquid is filtered and recycled, or collected for disposal, significantly reducing water volume.

A garment cleaning system that employs a fine mist of water containing specialized, fabric-safe, marine-derived or inspired chelating agents. These agents are designed to selectively bind to metallic ions, mineral deposits (e.g., from hard water stains), and certain organic pollutants commonly found in dirt and stains. Once chelated, the contaminants become more soluble or easily dislodged, allowing for effective removal with significantly reduced water rinsing, which is then filtered to remove the chelated compounds for safe disposal or recovery.

A targeted spray or fine mist system that applies a fabric-safe mixture of biofilm-dispersing enzymes, mild natural dispersants, or lytic bacteriophages onto garments. This treatment specifically breaks down the sticky matrix of microbial biofilms and the embedded dirt/odor compounds, allowing them to be easily wiped away with a damp cloth or lifted by a gentle air current and filtration system, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing to eliminate persistent smells and grime.

A smart appliance or handheld device that uses optical sensors to detect stains. It then precisely "inkjets" micro-droplets of a concentrated, fabric-safe cleaning solution onto the stain. After a brief dwell time, a focused burst of warm air or a micro-vacuum system rapidly evaporates the liquid and lifts the dissolved/suspended dirt, requiring minimal cleaning fluid and no bulk water rinsing.

A minimal-water washing chamber where clothes are briefly exposed to a mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution. Pulsed electric fields are then applied across the solution and fabric. These pulses disrupt the integrity of microbial biofilms (which encase much of the dirt and odor-causing bacteria) and weaken the electrostatic or cohesive bonds of embedded dirt particles, making them easier to detach and rinse away with significantly less water and agitation.

Integrate a bioluminescent detection system into a laundry appliance or garment cabinet. After a minimal-water cleaning cycle (e.g., misting, plasma), a mild, fabric-safe bioluminescent agent is briefly applied or activated. If significant organic residues (like bacteria, body oils) remain, they trigger a light emission, indicating the need for further cleaning or a more intensive approach. This smart feedback loop ensures that clothes are only cleaned as much as necessary, significantly reducing unnecessary water consumption.

A washing device where garments are exposed to a minimal, thin film of a specialized liquid containing stable micro- or nano-bubbles (or precursors). Precisely tuned, low-power ultrasonic transducers are then activated, causing these bubbles to rapidly oscillate, expand, and contract in place. This generates highly localized, gentle yet effective "micro-scrubbing" forces directly at the fabric-dirt interface, dislodging contaminants without requiring large volumes of water or bulk mechanical agitation. The dirty film is then easily wiped or vacuumed away.

A sealed garment cabinet that generates a fine, electrostatically charged mist of ultra-pure water (or a mild cleaning solution). These charged nano-droplets are engineered to act as "dirt nuclei," preferentially attracting and encapsulating fine particulate dirt, lint, and odor molecules from the garments via electrostatic forces and targeted surface chemistry. Once sufficiently agglomerated and weighted with contaminants, a controlled electrostatic field or gentle air current causes these dirt-laden droplets to coalesce and precipitate onto a collection surface at the bottom of the chamber, effectively "raining" the dirt out of the fabric without wetting the garment or requiring mechanical action.

A controlled environment cabinet or low-humidity wash chamber that applies a fine, fabric-safe mist containing targeted fungal enzymes or specific fungal spore extracts. These enzymes, under optimized temperature and humidity conditions, specifically target and degrade stubborn organic stains (e.g., grass, wine, oil) and complex odor-causing compounds embedded in fabric. This breaks the stains down into smaller, water-soluble, or volatile molecules that are easily wiped away or dissipated by gentle airflow, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing and harsh chemicals for tough stains.

A subsequent change (e.g., mild heating or pH neutralization) causes the fibers to shrink, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration system, achieving cleaning with very low water input.

A low-water washing system that utilizes a highly concentrated, yet gentle, biodegradable biosurfactant foam. Garments are placed in a chamber where a precise, minimal amount of water, cleaning agents, and biosurfactant is agitated to create a dense, stable foam. Clothes are gently tumbled through this foam, allowing the biosurfactants to lift and emulsify dirt with minimal bulk water. The foam is then collapsed, and the concentrated dirty liquid is filtered and recycled, or collected for disposal, significantly reducing water volume.

A garment cleaning system that employs a fine mist of water containing specialized, fabric-safe, marine-derived or inspired chelating agents. These agents are designed to selectively bind to metallic ions, mineral deposits (e.g., from hard water stains), and certain organic pollutants commonly found in dirt and stains. Once chelated, the contaminants become more soluble or easily dislodged, allowing for effective removal with significantly reduced water rinsing, which is then filtered to remove the chelated compounds for safe disposal or recovery.

A targeted spray or fine mist system that applies a fabric-safe mixture of biofilm-dispersing enzymes, mild natural dispersants, or lytic bacteriophages onto garments. This treatment specifically breaks down the sticky matrix of microbial biofilms and the embedded dirt/odor compounds, allowing them to be easily wiped away with a damp cloth or lifted by a gentle air current and filtration system, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing to eliminate persistent smells and grime.

A smart appliance or handheld device that uses optical sensors to detect stains. It then precisely "inkjets" micro-droplets of a concentrated, fabric-safe cleaning solution onto the stain. After a brief dwell time, a focused burst of warm air or a micro-vacuum system rapidly evaporates the liquid and lifts the dissolved/suspended dirt, requiring minimal cleaning fluid and no bulk water rinsing.

A minimal-water washing chamber where clothes are briefly exposed to a mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution. Pulsed electric fields are then applied across the solution and fabric. These pulses disrupt the integrity of microbial biofilms (which encase much of the dirt and odor-causing bacteria) and weaken the electrostatic or cohesive bonds of embedded dirt particles, making them easier to detach and rinse away with significantly less water and agitation.

Integrate a bioluminescent detection system into a laundry appliance or garment cabinet. After a minimal-water cleaning cycle (e.g., misting, plasma), a mild, fabric-safe bioluminescent agent is briefly applied or activated. If significant organic residues (like bacteria, body oils) remain, they trigger a light emission, indicating the need for further cleaning or a more intensive approach. This smart feedback loop ensures that clothes are only cleaned as much as necessary, significantly reducing unnecessary water consumption.

A washing device where garments are exposed to a minimal, thin film of a specialized liquid containing stable micro- or nano-bubbles (or precursors). Precisely tuned, low-power ultrasonic transducers are then activated, causing these bubbles to rapidly oscillate, expand, and contract in place. This generates highly localized, gentle yet effective "micro-scrubbing" forces directly at the fabric-dirt interface, dislodging contaminants without requiring large volumes of water or bulk mechanical agitation. The dirty film is then easily wiped or vacuumed away.

A sealed garment cabinet that generates a fine, electrostatically charged mist of ultra-pure water (or a mild cleaning solution). These charged nano-droplets are engineered to act as "dirt nuclei," preferentially attracting and encapsulating fine particulate dirt, lint, and odor molecules from the garments via electrostatic forces and targeted surface chemistry. Once sufficiently agglomerated and weighted with contaminants, a controlled electrostatic field or gentle air current causes these dirt-laden droplets to coalesce and precipitate onto a collection surface at the bottom of the chamber, effectively "raining" the dirt out of the fabric without wetting the garment or requiring mechanical action.

A controlled environment cabinet or low-humidity wash chamber that applies a fine, fabric-safe mist containing targeted fungal enzymes or specific fungal spore extracts. These enzymes, under optimized temperature and humidity conditions, specifically target and degrade stubborn organic stains (e.g., grass, wine, oil) and complex odor-causing compounds embedded in fabric. This breaks the stains down into smaller, water-soluble, or volatile molecules that are easily wiped away or dissipated by gentle airflow, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing and harsh chemicals for tough stains.

When the field is removed, the fluid instantly thins, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then carried away by filtration. The fluid is continuously recycled and purified for subsequent uses with minimal loss and no water.

During a brief cycle with a very fine, minimal mist of water, this sheet actively attracts and captures body oils, dissolved dirt, and fine particulate matter released from the garments. The superhydrophilic material "wicks" and holds these contaminants, effectively cleaning the clothes with minimal water, and the sheet is then rinsed clean for reuse.
included_members.abstraction: Minimal-moisture mobilization: Use of a very small, fine application of water to solubilize or loosen oils and particulates so they can be transferred to the capture medium without bulk washing.

The wetted garment is then gently frozen (e.g., with chilled air) and placed in a low-pressure chamber. The frozen cleaning solution and dirt sublimate away, removing contaminants directly from the fabric structure without liquid drainage or mechanical stress, resulting in clean, dry clothes with minimal water usage.
included_members.abstraction: Minimal-wetting, non-mechanical cleaning interface: Limit wetting to surface-level coverage (e.g., fine mist), use chemical encapsulation or solubilization at very low liquid volumes, and avoid agitation or centrifugal drainage to reduce fabric stress and water usage.

included_members.description: Application system that delivers a controlled, minimal quantity of an activating agent (e.g., pH-tuned mist or humidity) to engage the responsive components locally.
included_members.explanation: Delivers a minimal, localized activating mist/humidity to trigger cleaning action—minimal-water spot activation.

included_members.idea_text: A low-water washing system that utilizes a highly concentrated, yet gentle, biodegradable biosurfactant foam. Garments are placed in a chamber where a precise, minimal amount of water, cleaning agents, and biosurfactant is agitated to create a dense, stable foam. Clothes are gently tumbled through this foam, allowing the biosurfactants to lift and emulsify dirt with minimal bulk water. The foam is then collapsed, and the concentrated dirty liquid is filtered and recycled, or collected for disposal, significantly reducing water volume.
included_members.abstraction: Dense biosurfactant-based foam as primary cleaning medium: Generate a stable, highly concentrated foam of biodegradable biosurfactants that lifts and emulsifies soils while using little bulk water.
included_members.label: Dense biosurfactant-based foam as primary cleaning medium
included_members.description: Generate a stable, highly concentrated foam of biodegradable biosurfactants that lifts and emulsifies soils while using little bulk water.
included_members.explanation: Uses dense biosurfactant foam to clean with very little water—minimal-water foam-based wet cleaning.

included_members.idea_text: A low-water washing system that utilizes a highly concentrated, yet gentle, biodegradable biosurfactant foam. Garments are placed in a chamber where a precise, minimal amount of water, cleaning agents, and biosurfactant is agitated to create a dense, stable foam. Clothes are gently tumbled through this foam, allowing the biosurfactants to lift and emulsify dirt with minimal bulk water. The foam is then collapsed, and the concentrated dirty liquid is filtered and recycled, or collected for disposal, significantly reducing water volume.
included_members.abstraction: Controlled agitation/tumbling in a confined foam-filled chamber: Move garments through the foam under gentle, metered agitation to maximize contact and transfer of dirt into the dispersed phase without excess water.
included_members.label: Controlled agitation/tumbling in a confined foam-filled chamber
included_members.description: Move garments through the foam under gentle, metered agitation to maximize contact and transfer of dirt into the dispersed phase without excess water.
included_members.explanation: Tumbling/agitation within a foam-filled chamber to increase contact while keeping liquid low—minimal-water foam process.

The foam is then collapsed, and the concentrated dirty liquid is filtered and recycled, or collected for disposal, significantly reducing water volume.
included_members.abstraction: Foam collapse and concentrated fluid separation for reuse: Collapse the foam to produce a small volume of concentrated dirty liquid, then filter/separate contaminants and either recycle cleaning agents or collect waste.
included_members.label: Foam collapse and concentrated fluid separation for reuse
included_members.description: Collapse the foam to produce a small volume of concentrated dirty liquid, then filter/separate contaminants and either recycle cleaning agents or collect waste.
included_members.explanation: Collapses foam to a small dirty liquid volume for separation/reuse—still part of minimal-water foam cleaning workflow.

included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning system that employs a fine mist of water containing specialized, fabric-safe, marine-derived or inspired chelating agents. These agents are designed to selectively bind to metallic ions, mineral deposits (e.g., from hard water stains), and certain organic pollutants commonly found in dirt and stains. Once chelated, the contaminants become more soluble or easily dislodged, allowing for effective removal with significantly reduced water rinsing, which is then filtered to remove the chelated compounds for safe disposal or recovery.
included_members.abstraction: Selective chelation of contaminants to increase solubility/remove adhesion: Use agents that bind specific ions/mineral deposits and certain organics so those contaminants become more soluble or detach easily under minimal water action.
included_members.label: Selective chelation of contaminants to increase solubility/remove adhesion
included_members.description: Use agents that bind specific ions/mineral deposits and certain organics so those contaminants become more soluble or detach easily under minimal water action.
included_members.explanation: Chelation is a chemistry aid intended to enable cleaning under minimal water conditions rather than bulk washing.

included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning system that employs a fine mist of water containing specialized, fabric-safe, marine-derived or inspired chelating agents. These agents are designed to selectively bind to metallic ions, mineral deposits (e.g., from hard water stains), and certain organic pollutants commonly found in dirt and stains. Once chelated, the contaminants become more soluble or easily dislodged, allowing for effective removal with significantly reduced water rinsing, which is then filtered to remove the chelated compounds for safe disposal or recovery.
included_members.abstraction: Fine mist/low-volume spray delivery: Generate and apply a controlled fine mist of the formulation to wet fabric surfaces with low overall water usage while ensuring surface coverage and penetration.
included_members.label: Fine mist/low-volume spray delivery
included_members.description: Generate and apply a controlled fine mist of the formulation to wet fabric surfaces with low overall water usage while ensuring surface coverage and penetration.
included_members.explanation: Fine mist/low-volume spray is explicitly minimal-water localized wet cleaning.

included_members.idea_text: A targeted spray or fine mist system that applies a fabric-safe mixture of biofilm-dispersing enzymes, mild natural dispersants, or lytic bacteriophages onto garments. This treatment specifically breaks down the sticky matrix of microbial biofilms and the embedded dirt/odor compounds, allowing them to be easily wiped away with a damp cloth or lifted by a gentle air current and filtration system, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing to eliminate persistent smells and grime.
included_members.abstraction: Precision spray/mist delivery: A delivery mechanism that creates a controlled fine mist or directed spray to apply small volumes of treatment accurately to contaminated areas.
included_members.label: Precision spray/mist delivery
included_members.description: A delivery mechanism that creates a controlled fine mist or directed spray to apply small volumes of treatment accurately to contaminated areas.
included_members.explanation: Precision mist/spray applies small liquid volumes locally—minimal-water localized wet cleaning.

included_members.idea_text: A smart appliance or handheld device that uses optical sensors to detect stains. It then precisely "inkjets" micro-droplets of a concentrated, fabric-safe cleaning solution onto the stain. After a brief dwell time, a focused burst of warm air or a micro-vacuum system rapidly evaporates the liquid and lifts the dissolved/suspended dirt, requiring minimal cleaning fluid and no bulk water rinsing.
included_members.abstraction: Targeted micro-dispensing of concentrated cleaning agent: Precisely deposit metered, high-concentration cleaning micro-droplets only onto detected stains to provide required chemistry with minimal liquid volume.
included_members.label: Targeted micro-dispensing of concentrated cleaning agent
included_members.description: Precisely deposit metered, high-concentration cleaning micro-droplets only onto detected stains to provide required chemistry with minimal liquid volume.
included_members.explanation: Micro-dispensed droplets for spot cleaning are minimal-water localized wet cleaning.

included_members.idea_text: A smart appliance or handheld device that uses optical sensors to detect stains. It then precisely "inkjets" micro-droplets of a concentrated, fabric-safe cleaning solution onto the stain. After a brief dwell time, a focused burst of warm air or a micro-vacuum system rapidly evaporates the liquid and lifts the dissolved/suspended dirt, requiring minimal cleaning fluid and no bulk water rinsing.
included_members.abstraction: Localized thermal and suction extraction: Remove applied fluid and mobilized soil by combining focused heating/evaporation and targeted vacuum/extraction at the spot.
included_members.label: Localized thermal and suction extraction
included_members.description: Remove applied fluid and mobilized soil by combining focused heating/evaporation and targeted vacuum/extraction at the spot.
included_members.explanation: Localized heating plus suction to remove small applied fluid volumes supports minimal-water spot wet cleaning without full rinsing.

included_members.idea_text: A minimal-water washing chamber where clothes are briefly exposed to a mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution. Pulsed electric fields are then applied across the solution and fabric. These pulses disrupt the integrity of microbial biofilms (which encase much of the dirt and odor-causing bacteria) and weaken the electrostatic or cohesive bonds of embedded dirt particles, making them easier to detach and rinse away with significantly less water and agitation.
included_members.abstraction: Brief low-volume aqueous conditioning: Expose fabrics to a small volume of mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution for a short time to loosen soils/biofilms before active disruption.
included_members.label: Brief low-volume aqueous conditioning
included_members.description: Expose fabrics to a small volume of mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution for a short time to loosen soils/biofilms before active disruption.
included_members.explanation: Brief low-volume aqueous conditioning is a minimal-water wet pre-treatment.

included_members.idea_text: A minimal-water washing chamber where clothes are briefly exposed to a mild, fabric-safe aqueous solution. Pulsed electric fields are then applied across the solution and fabric. These pulses disrupt the integrity of microbial biofilms (which encase much of the dirt and odor-causing bacteria) and weaken the electrostatic or cohesive bonds of embedded dirt particles, making them easier to detach and rinse away with significantly less water and agitation.
included_members.abstraction: Reduced-volume rinse and low-agitation removal: Use focused rinsing, low flow volumes, and limited mechanical agitation after disruption to carry away detached material efficiently.
included_members.label: Reduced-volume rinse and low-agitation removal
included_members.description: Use focused rinsing, low flow volumes, and limited mechanical agitation after disruption to carry away detached material efficiently.
included_members.explanation: Reduced-volume, targeted rinsing is explicitly minimal-water localized wet cleaning/removal.

included_members.idea_text: Integrate a bioluminescent detection system into a laundry appliance or garment cabinet. After a minimal-water cleaning cycle (e.g., misting, plasma), a mild, fabric-safe bioluminescent agent is briefly applied or activated. If significant organic residues (like bacteria, body oils) remain, they trigger a light emission, indicating the need for further cleaning or a more intensive approach. This smart feedback loop ensures that clothes are only cleaned as much as necessary, significantly reducing unnecessary water consumption.
included_members.abstraction: Minimal-water cleaning process: A cleaning step that removes soil with very little water (e.g., misting, plasma, steam, ultrasonic) used as the default/first-pass treatment.
included_members.label: Minimal-water cleaning process
included_members.description: A cleaning step that removes soil with very little water (e.g., misting, plasma, steam, ultrasonic) used as the default/first-pass treatment.
included_members.explanation: Default low-water modalities like misting/steam/ultrasonic align with minimal-water localized wet cleaning approaches.

included_members.idea_text: A washing device where garments are exposed to a minimal, thin film of a specialized liquid containing stable micro- or nano-bubbles (or precursors). Precisely tuned, low-power ultrasonic transducers are then activated, causing these bubbles to rapidly oscillate, expand, and contract in place. This generates highly localized, gentle yet effective "micro-scrubbing" forces directly at the fabric-dirt interface, dislodging contaminants without requiring large volumes of water or bulk mechanical agitation. The dirty film is then easily wiped or vacuumed away.
included_members.abstraction: Ultrasonic-driven oscillatory bubble micro-scrubbing: Drive stabilized micro- or nano-bubbles (or precursors) in a thin liquid film with low-power, tuned ultrasound so bubbles oscillate and produce highly localized expansion/contraction forces that mechanically dislodge contaminants at the fabric surface.
included_members.label: Ultrasonic-driven oscillatory bubble micro-scrubbing
included_members.description: Drive stabilized micro- or nano-bubbles (or precursors) in a thin liquid film with low-power, tuned ultrasound so bubbles oscillate and produce highly localized expansion/contraction forces that mechanically dislodge contaminants at the fabric surface.
included_members.explanation: Uses micro/nano-bubbles in a thin liquid film with ultrasound for localized low-water cleaning.

included_members.idea_text: A washing device where garments are exposed to a minimal, thin film of a specialized liquid containing stable micro- or nano-bubbles (or precursors). Precisely tuned, low-power ultrasonic transducers are then activated, causing these bubbles to rapidly oscillate, expand, and contract in place. This generates highly localized, gentle yet effective "micro-scrubbing" forces directly at the fabric-dirt interface, dislodging contaminants without requiring large volumes of water or bulk mechanical agitation. The dirty film is then easily wiped or vacuumed away.
included_members.abstraction: Stabilized microscopic bubble/precursor structures as transducers: Use chemically or physically stabilized micro/nano-bubbles or precursors suspended in a minimal liquid to act as the medium that couples external acoustic energy into local mechanical action.
included_members.label: Stabilized microscopic bubble/precursor structures as transducers
included_members.description: Use chemically or physically stabilized micro/nano-bubbles or precursors suspended in a minimal liquid to act as the medium that couples external acoustic energy into local mechanical action.
included_members.explanation: Stabilized micro/nano-bubbles in minimal liquid act as the localized wet-cleaning medium.

included_members.idea_text: A washing device where garments are exposed to a minimal, thin film of a specialized liquid containing stable micro- or nano-bubbles (or precursors). Precisely tuned, low-power ultrasonic transducers are then activated, causing these bubbles to rapidly oscillate, expand, and contract in place. This generates highly localized, gentle yet effective "micro-scrubbing" forces directly at the fabric-dirt interface, dislodging contaminants without requiring large volumes of water or bulk mechanical agitation. The dirty film is then easily wiped or vacuumed away.
included_members.abstraction: Thin-film application plus non-rinse removal: Apply a minimal, thin liquid film to garments and remove the now-contaminated film by wiping, vacuuming, or similar collection methods instead of bulk rinsing.
included_members.label: Thin-film application plus non-rinse removal
included_members.description: Apply a minimal, thin liquid film to garments and remove the now-contaminated film by wiping, vacuuming, or similar collection methods instead of bulk rinsing.
included_members.explanation: Applies a thin film and removes it without rinsing—minimal-water localized wet cleaning.

included_members.idea_text: A sealed garment cabinet that generates a fine, electrostatically charged mist of ultra-pure water (or a mild cleaning solution). These charged nano-droplets are engineered to act as "dirt nuclei," preferentially attracting and encapsulating fine particulate dirt, lint, and odor molecules from the garments via electrostatic forces and targeted surface chemistry. Once sufficiently agglomerated and weighted with contaminants, a controlled electrostatic field or gentle air current causes these dirt-laden droplets to coalesce and precipitate onto a collection surface at the bottom of the chamber, effectively "raining" the dirt out of the fabric without wetting the garment or requiring mechanical action.
included_members.abstraction: Dose and droplet control to avoid fabric wetting: Manage droplet size, charge, concentration, and exposure time so contaminants transfer to droplets without saturating or soaking the textile fibers.
included_members.label: Dose and droplet control to avoid fabric wetting
included_members.description: Manage droplet size, charge, concentration, and exposure time so contaminants transfer to droplets without saturating or soaking the textile fibers.
included_members.explanation: Controls nano/micro-droplet dosing to clean without soaking—minimal-water mist/aerosol-style wetting avoidance.

included_members.idea_text: A controlled environment cabinet or low-humidity wash chamber that applies a fine, fabric-safe mist containing targeted fungal enzymes or specific fungal spore extracts. These enzymes, under optimized temperature and humidity conditions, specifically target and degrade stubborn organic stains (e.g., grass, wine, oil) and complex odor-causing compounds embedded in fabric. This breaks the stains down into smaller, water-soluble, or volatile molecules that are easily wiped away or dissipated by gentle airflow, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing and harsh chemicals for tough stains.
included_members.abstraction: Fine-mist delivery system: Apply actives as a fabric-safe aerosol or mist to achieve localized, minimal-liquid coverage and even distribution over targeted soiled areas.
included_members.label: Fine-mist delivery system
included_members.description: Apply actives as a fabric-safe aerosol or mist to achieve localized, minimal-liquid coverage and even distribution over targeted soiled areas.
included_members.explanation: Applies actives via fine mist for localized minimal-liquid coverage—thin-film/mist cleaning.

nodes.name: Dry mechanical or aerodynamic particle removal
nodes.description: Detach and extract dry particulates via brushing, microstructures, vibration, suction, or directed airflow.
idea_text: A specialized laundry treatment system where clothes are exposed to a controlled blast of fine dry ice pellets. The sublimation effect physically removes embedded dirt and grime, similar to agitation but without any water, making it ideal for certain fabrics or for quick refresh cycles where water isn't necessary.

A laundry drum or chamber equipped with high-efficiency vacuum nozzles and brushes. Clothes are tumbled while a powerful vacuum system actively lifts and extracts dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial dry dirt from the fabric. This process also helps remove airborne particles and can extend the life of garments between full wet washes.

A specialized garment cleaning chamber that briefly chills clothes to cryogenic temperatures (e.g., using a controlled blast of chilled air or liquid nitrogen vapor). This causes embedded dirt, chewing gum, or stubborn stains to become brittle, allowing them to be easily dislodged and vibrated or brushed off the fabric without the need for water or solvents.

A specialized laundry chamber or drum designed with precisely positioned nozzles that generate high-velocity, controlled air vortices around and through the garments. These aerodynamic forces would gently lift and carry away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial particulate dirt from fabric fibers, collecting them in a filter system, effectively de-soiling clothes without any water.

A garment cleaning chamber that exposes clothes to precisely tuned mechanical vibrations or sonic frequencies. These frequencies are engineered to resonate with the physical bonds between dirt particles and fabric fibers, effectively loosening and detaching dirt without requiring bulk water. The dislodged particles are then collected by a vacuum or filtration system.

A handheld device or an automated robotic system with a specialized roller or pad whose surface mimics the micro- or nano-structure of gecko feet. This roller would be gently passed over garments, picking up dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial grime through contact. The collected dirt would then be released from the roller's surface into a waste receptacle (e.g., by a slight change in angle or pressure), allowing the cleaning surface to be reused repeatedly without water or chemicals.

Develop garments or specialized fabric liners with embedded or woven piezoelectric fibers. When these garments are placed in a dry tumbling drum, the gentle mechanical motion of tumbling induces micro-vibrations within the fabric itself (due to the piezoelectric effect). These self-generated, high-frequency vibrations effectively loosen and dislodge dry dirt, dust, and lint particles from the fibers, which are then collected by an integrated vacuum and filter system within the drum, eliminating the need for water for general refreshing.

A specialized enclosed chamber where garments are suspended and gently agitated by powerful, non-audible ultrasonic standing waves. This contactless "tumbling" and manipulation effectively loosens dry dirt, dust, and lint from the fabric fibers. A gentle filtered airflow simultaneously draws away the dislodged particles into a collection system, providing a dry, contact-free cleaning and refreshing process without any water or mechanical wear on the fabric.

A garment refresh chamber where clothes are exposed to a specific low-temperature plasma (e.g., derived from oxygen or hydrogen precursor gases). This plasma generates energetic reactive species tuned to gently react with and break down organic residues (body oils, odors, superficial grime) on the fabric surface. These contaminants are converted into volatile byproducts that are then vacuumed away, providing a deep, dry clean at a molecular level without water or harsh chemicals, thereby extending garment life.

Design a laundry appliance with a rotating drum or series of pads equipped with precisely engineered, fabric-safe micro-bristles and combs, mimicking insect grooming structures. As clothes tumble or pass through, these structures gently brush, comb, and scrape away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial grime from fabric fibers, collecting them in an integrated vacuum system, thus cleaning without water.

A garment cleaning chamber equipped with multi-modal transducers capable of generating a broadband spectrum of mechanical waves, including both compressional and shear waves, that propagate through the fabric. These complex vibrations are designed to physically agitate and break the adhesion of diverse dirt particles (dry dust, sticky grime) from fibers across various fabric types. Dislodged particles are then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration system, achieving dry cleaning without specific reliance on a single resonance.

A garment cleaning system where a very fine, dry, and biodegradable micro-abrasive powder (e.g., cellulose beads) is gently dusted onto clothes. A precisely controlled, low-power pulsed laser beam then scans the fabric. The laser energy interacts with the micro-abrasive particles, causing them to gently 'lift' or 'etch' away dirt and grime from the fabric surface through localized photomechanical action. The dirty micro-abrasive is then vacuumed away, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.

A garment cleaning system where a low-power, pulsed infrared laser scans the fabric. The laser energy is tuned to be preferentially absorbed by dirt particles or the interface layer, causing rapid, localized thermal expansion and contraction. This generates micro-scale mechanical shockwaves that break the adhesive bonds of dirt particles, which are then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.

A garment chamber where clothes are exposed to precisely tuned RF or microwave fields. The frequency and power are optimized to selectively heat and slightly expand/soften the dirt particles or the interface layer between dirt and fabric, without significantly heating the fabric itself. This localized thermal stress, combined with gentle mechanical tumbling or air currents, causes the dirt to lose adhesion and be dislodged. A filtration system then collects the removed particles, providing a water-free cleaning method.

A sealed garment cleaning chamber where clothes are suspended. An array of micro-jets or pulsators generates highly localized, tunable air pressure pulsations around individual fabric fibers. These rapid, non-linear air movements create micro-turbulences and pressure differentials that physically dislodge dry dirt, dust, and lint particles without harsh mechanical contact or significant bulk air movement. Dislodged particles are then quietly drawn into a filter system by a very gentle, continuous background flow.

Garments are treated with a dissolvable or detachable nanocoating that has a stronger affinity for dirt/oils than for fabric fibers. After wear, the garments are placed in a gentle tumbling drum or cabinet. A mild, fabric-safe trigger (e.g., a specific light wavelength, a slight humidity change, or a very mild vibration) causes the nanocoating to rapidly delaminate or de-bond from the fabric, encapsulating and releasing the accumulated dirt. The shed nanocoating and dirt particles are then collected by a vacuum and filter system, leaving clean fabric with no water.

A specialized cleaning plate or drum lining made of a piezoelectric material. Clothes are gently pressed against or tumbled on this surface. Interdigitated electrodes on the surface generate high-frequency SAWs that propagate along the interface with the fabric. These SAWs exert precise, localized mechanical forces on dirt particles at the fabric surface, effectively "sweeping" or "vibrating" them off without needing bulk water, solvents, or bulk ultrasonic cavitation. The dislodged dirt is collected by an integrated vacuum system.

A laundry appliance with internal surfaces or rotating pads featuring arrays of soft, fabric-safe micro-needles or textured micro-projections. As garments are gently tumbled or brushed against these surfaces, the micro-needles penetrate the weave, physically lifting and extracting deeply embedded dirt, dust, and particulate matter from the fabric pores without requiring water or harsh chemicals.

A cleaning chamber where garments are introduced and suspended on a precisely controlled air cushion (an "air film") generated from below. This eliminates friction and mechanical wear. While suspended, targeted, high-velocity air nozzles (acting as siphons or localized vacuums) are directed at the garment from above, actively lifting and extracting dry dust, lint, and superficial grime from the fabric fibers, collecting them in a filter system, all without water or direct contact.

A sealed garment cabinet or tumbling drum equipped with a heating and cooling system to create a controlled temperature gradient across the fabric surface in a dry environment. As garments are gently tumbled or suspended, the temperature gradient induces thermophoretic forces that gently drive fine dust, lint, and superficial particulate dirt away from the warmer fabric surface towards a colder collection plate or filter, effectively removing dry contaminants without water.

A garment refreshing cabinet where an internal electric field generates a controlled "ion wind" or electrohydrodynamic flow. This silent, gentle, localized air current is directed across the fabric surfaces, physically dislodging dry dust, lint, and carrying away odor molecules without any moving mechanical parts. The dislodged particles and odors are then collected by an integrated filter and purification system, providing a water-free and gentle cleaning method.

Garments are woven with a percentage of specialized, micro-scale stimuli-responsive fibers (e.g., pH or humidity-sensitive polymers). When the garment is exposed to a minimal, fine mist of water with a specific pH, these embedded fibers swell, physically pushing outwards and dislodging dirt particles from the fabric structure. A subsequent change (e.g., mild heating or pH neutralization) causes the fibers to shrink, releasing the loosened dirt, which is then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration system, achieving cleaning with very low water input.

A sealed garment cabinet where clothes are suspended. Compressed air is fed into an array of miniature vortex tubes directed at the garments. The resulting high-velocity, temperature-differentiated air streams create targeted aerodynamic forces to dislodge dry dust and lint (mechanical cleaning) and simultaneously generate localized thermophoretic effects, pushing fine particles away from the fabric towards a collection filter. This provides a dry, water-free, and energy-efficient cleaning process.

A specialized garment refresh chamber where clothes are briefly exposed to a controlled, low-energy electron beam. The electron beam's energy is tuned to target and disrupt the molecular bonds of organic dirt, oils, and odor-causing compounds on the fabric surface. These contaminants are then converted into volatile byproducts or easily detachable fragments that are removed by a gentle vacuum system, providing a deep, dry, and chemical-free surface cleaning and deodorization, minimizing the need for water washes.

A garment cleaning station equipped with a low-power, pulsed laser system. Optical sensors identify soiled areas, and the laser is precisely tuned (wavelength, pulse energy) to be selectively absorbed by common dirt, oils, or stain chromophores. The absorbed energy causes rapid, localized micro-vaporization or thermal decomposition of the contaminant, effectively "ablating" it from the fabric surface without heating or damaging the surrounding fibers. A gentle vacuum collects the resulting microscopic debris, providing an extremely targeted, water-free, and residue-free cleaning method.

A targeted spray or fine mist system that applies a fabric-safe mixture of biofilm-dispersing enzymes, mild natural dispersants, or lytic bacteriophages onto garments. This treatment specifically breaks down the sticky matrix of microbial biofilms and the embedded dirt/odor compounds, allowing them to be easily wiped away with a damp cloth or lifted by a gentle air current and filtration system, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing to eliminate persistent smells and grime.

A specialized laundry drum or cabinet with embedded micro-electrodes near the fabric surface. When clothes are present, a precisely controlled, short, high-energy electrical pulse is applied. This generates localized, micro-scale mechanical shockwaves within the fabric itself or at the fabric-dirt interface, effectively breaking the adhesive bonds of embedded dirt and grime without damaging the fibers. The dislodged particles are then removed by a gentle vacuum and filtration system, providing a water-free cleaning method that targets deeply embedded contaminants.

Design a laundry drum that tumbles clothes in a low-humidity environment, inducing an electrostatic charge on both fabric and dirt particles. The charged dirt particles are then attracted to an oppositely charged collector plate or filter within the drum, effectively "lifting" them off the fabric without water.

A sealed garment cabinet designed to gently heat clothes to a precisely controlled, low temperature in a dry, inert atmosphere. This controlled heating causes volatile odor-causing compounds, body oils, and light organic residues embedded in the fabric to desorb (vaporize) from the fibers. A continuous, gentle airflow then carries these volatilized contaminants to a filtration or catalytic oxidation unit for capture and safe breakdown, effectively refreshing and deodorizing garments without the use of water or chemicals, extending wear time between wet washes.

A highly specialized garment cleaning station equipped with a low-energy, broad, non-damaging ion beam. Optical sensors identify and map individual dirt particles or stains. The ion beam is then directed to these specific micro-regions, where the kinetic energy of the ions physically dislodges and sputters away the contaminant molecules from the fabric surface without damaging the fibers. A gentle vacuum system collects the sputtered debris, providing an ultra-precise, water-free, and residue-free spot cleaning method.

Design a laundry drum with an internal lining composed of a dense array of very fine, compliant, and electrically charged polymeric filaments or a specialized mesh. As clothes tumble, these filaments gently brush against the fabric, and the static charge passively attracts and entangles dry dust, lint, and pet hair. The collected debris adheres to the filaments, which are periodically retracted and vibrated or subjected to a reverse charge to release the accumulated dirt into a separate collection bin, providing a gentle, water-free dry cleaning and de-linting process.

A flat cleaning surface or a drum lining integrated with an array of microscopic, fabric-safe MEMS actuators. When a garment makes contact, optical sensors identify individual dirt particles. The micro-actuators then precisely extend or vibrate locally, gently lifting or dislodging specific dirt particles from the fabric fibers. These particles are then drawn away by a localized micro-vacuum system, enabling highly targeted, dry, and extremely gentle particulate removal from clothing without water.

A garment cleaning system where clothes are briefly exposed to a very fine mist of a fabric-safe, non-toxic, supersaturated crystalline salt solution. Cycles of controlled humidity reduction and re-humidification are then applied in a dry chamber. As the salt crystals grow within the fabric pores and around dirt particles, they exert micro-mechanical stresses. When humidity changes, they re-crystallize or shrink, causing embedded dirt to physically detach from the fibers. The loosened dirt and salt residue are then removed by a gentle vacuum and filtration system, achieving cleaning with minimal water and no harsh chemicals.

Garments are manufactured with embedded or surface-applied microscopic, optically responsive elements (e.g., plasmonic nanoparticles or specialized polymer fibers). When placed in a dry cleaning chamber and illuminated with precisely tuned, non-damaging light wavelengths, these elements preferentially absorb energy. This causes rapid, localized micro-thermal expansion and contraction or phase change directly at the fabric-dirt interface, physically agitating and dislodging dirt particles. A gentle airflow then removes the loosened particles, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method leveraging engineered fabric properties.

A garment refreshing cabinet with internal curved surfaces and precisely angled air nozzles designed to exploit the Coandă effect. A continuous, laminar sheet of high-velocity air is generated and directed to flow smoothly over the garments. This non-turbulent, wall-attached airflow creates a gentle, continuous shear force across the fabric surfaces, effectively lifting and carrying away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial particulate matter without harsh mechanical contact. The dirt-laden air is then silently directed into a high-efficiency filter system, providing a very gentle, water-free cleaning and deodorizing method.

A controlled environment cabinet or low-humidity wash chamber that applies a fine, fabric-safe mist containing targeted fungal enzymes or specific fungal spore extracts. These enzymes, under optimized temperature and humidity conditions, specifically target and degrade stubborn organic stains (e.g., grass, wine, oil) and complex odor-causing compounds embedded in fabric. This breaks the stains down into smaller, water-soluble, or volatile molecules that are easily wiped away or dissipated by gentle airflow, significantly reducing the need for bulk water washing and harsh chemicals for tough stains.

Design a laundry drum that tumbles clothes in a low-humidity environment, inducing an electrostatic charge on both fabric and dirt particles. included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning chamber that exposes clothes to precisely tuned mechanical vibrations or sonic frequencies. These frequencies are engineered to resonate with the physical bonds between dirt particles and fabric fibers, effectively loosening and detaching dirt without requiring bulk water. The dislodged particles are then collected by a vacuum or filtration system.
included_members.abstraction: Resonant vibrational/acoustic agitation: Application of tuned mechanical vibrations or sonic frequencies that induce resonance at the dirt–fiber interface to break adhesive bonds and dislodge particles.
included_members.label: Resonant vibrational/acoustic agitation
included_members.description: Application of tuned mechanical vibrations or sonic frequencies that induce resonance at the dirt–fiber interface to break adhesive bonds and dislodge particles.
included_members.explanation: Resonant vibration/acoustics detach dry particles without bulk liquid—dry mechanical removal.

included_members.idea_text: A handheld device or an automated robotic system with a specialized roller or pad whose surface mimics the micro- or nano-structure of gecko feet. This roller would be gently passed over garments, picking up dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial grime through contact. The collected dirt would then be released from the roller's surface into a waste receptacle (e.g., by a slight change in angle or pressure), allowing the cleaning surface to be reused repeatedly without water or chemicals.
included_members.abstraction: Micro/nano-structured adhesive pickup surface: A surface patterned at micro- or nano-scale (gecko-like setae) that preferentially captures dry dust, lint, and hair on contact and holds particles via adhesion/van der Waals or mechanical interlocking until actively released.

included_members.description: A surface patterned at micro- or nano-scale (gecko-like setae) that preferentially captures dry dust, lint, and hair on contact and holds particles via adhesion/van der Waals or mechanical interlocking until actively released.
included_members.explanation: Dry-contact adhesive micro/nano surface removes dust/lint/hair without liquids, a dry mechanical particle removal method.

included_members.idea_text: Develop garments or specialized fabric liners with embedded or woven piezoelectric fibers. When these garments are placed in a dry tumbling drum, the gentle mechanical motion of tumbling induces micro-vibrations within the fabric itself (due to the piezoelectric effect). These self-generated, high-frequency vibrations effectively loosen and dislodge dry dirt, dust, and lint particles from the fibers, which are then collected by an integrated vacuum and filter system within the drum, eliminating the need for water for general refreshing.
included_members.abstraction: Embedded electromechanical actuation in textiles: Textile-integrated piezoelectric fibers or actuators that convert mechanical strain into high-frequency micro-vibrations inside the fabric structure to dislodge particles.
included_members.label: Embedded electromechanical actuation in textiles
included_members.description: Textile-integrated piezoelectric fibers or actuators that convert mechanical strain into high-frequency micro-vibrations inside the fabric structure to dislodge particles.
included_members.explanation: Micro-vibrations embedded in textiles dislodge particles mechanically, aligning with dry mechanical particle removal.

included_members.idea_text: A specialized enclosed chamber where garments are suspended and gently agitated by powerful, non-audible ultrasonic standing waves. This contactless "tumbling" and manipulation effectively loosens dry dirt, dust, and lint from the fabric fibers. A gentle filtered airflow simultaneously draws away the dislodged particles into a collection system, providing a dry, contact-free cleaning and refreshing process without any water or mechanical wear on the fabric.
included_members.abstraction: Gentle filtered airflow extraction: Low‑turbulence airflow routed across suspended garments to entrain and convey dislodged particles to a filtration/collection subsystem.
included_members.label: Gentle filtered airflow extraction
included_members.description: Low‑turbulence airflow routed across suspended garments to entrain and convey dislodged particles to a filtration/collection subsystem.
included_members.explanation: Filtered airflow entrains and removes loosened particles, fitting dry aerodynamic particle extraction.

included_members.idea_text: A garment refresh chamber where clothes are exposed to a specific low-temperature plasma (e.g., derived from oxygen or hydrogen precursor gases). This plasma generates energetic reactive species tuned to gently react with and break down organic residues (body oils, odors, superficial grime) on the fabric surface. These contaminants are converted into volatile byproducts that are then vacuumed away, providing a deep, dry clean at a molecular level without water or harsh chemicals, thereby extending garment life.
included_members.abstraction: Vacuum/airflow extraction of volatiles and particulates: maintain reduced pressure or directed flow to remove volatile byproducts and dislodged particles from the chamber before redeposition.
included_members.label: Vacuum/airflow extraction of volatiles and particulates
included_members.description: maintain reduced pressure or directed flow to remove volatile byproducts and dislodged particles from the chamber before redeposition.
included_members.explanation: Uses airflow/vacuum extraction to physically remove particulates/volatiles from the chamber (aerodynamic removal).

As clothes tumble or pass through, these structures gently brush, comb, and scrape away dry dust, lint, pet hair, and superficial grime from fabric fibers, collecting them in an integrated vacuum system, thus cleaning without water.

included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning chamber equipped with multi-modal transducers capable of generating a broadband spectrum of mechanical waves, including both compressional and shear waves, that propagate through the fabric. These complex vibrations are designed to physically agitate and break the adhesion of diverse dirt particles (dry dust, sticky grime) from fibers across various fabric types. Dislodged particles are then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration system, achieving dry cleaning without specific reliance on a single resonance.

included_members.label: Broadband mechanical-wave agitation (compressional + shear)
included_members.description: Produce and couple a broad spectrum of mechanical waves, including both compressional and shear components, through the textile to physically agitate fibers and detach varied soils without relying on a single resonance.
included_members.explanation: Mechanical-wave energy agitates fibers to detach soils without liquid immersion (dry physical removal).

included_members.explanation: Gentle airflow transports and captures dislodged dry particles via filtration/collection.

included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning system where a very fine, dry, and biodegradable micro-abrasive powder (e.g., cellulose beads) is gently dusted onto clothes. A precisely controlled, low-power pulsed laser beam then scans the fabric. The laser energy interacts with the micro-abrasive particles, causing them to gently 'lift' or 'etch' away dirt and grime from the fabric surface through localized photomechanical action. The dirty micro-abrasive is then vacuumed away, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.
included_members.abstraction: Energy–particle mediated mechanical detachment: Core process where externally applied energy couples to added particles to produce localized photomechanical action that lifts or etches away dirt from the substrate.
included_members.label: Energy–particle mediated mechanical detachment
included_members.description: Core process where externally applied energy couples to added particles to produce localized photomechanical action that lifts or etches away dirt from the substrate.
included_members.explanation: Detaches dirt via particle-assisted mechanical action (photomechanical) in a dry process.

included_members.description: Suction and filtration system that removes the contaminated particles from the fabric while containing and recovering waste.
included_members.explanation: Removes loosened soil/particles using suction and filtration—dry extraction.

included_members.idea_text: A garment cleaning system where a low-power, pulsed infrared laser scans the fabric. The laser energy is tuned to be preferentially absorbed by dirt particles or the interface layer, causing rapid, localized thermal expansion and contraction. This generates micro-scale mechanical shockwaves that break the adhesive bonds of dirt particles, which are then removed by a gentle airflow and filtration, providing a contactless, water-free cleaning method.
included_members.abstraction: Localized pulsed energy to produce detachment forces: Deliver short, localized energy pulses that are absorbed preferentially by dirt/interface to create forces that detach particles from the fabric.

included_members.explanation: Uses localized pulsed energy to mechanically detach dry particles from fabric.

included_members.idea_text: A garment chamber where clothes are exposed to precisely tuned RF or microwave fields. The frequency and power are optimized to selectively heat and slightly expand/soften the dirt particles or the interface layer between dirt and fabric, without significantly heating the fabric itself. This localized thermal stress, combined with gentle mechanical tumbling or air currents, causes the dirt to lose adhesion and be dislodged. A filtration system then collects the removed particles, providing a water-free cleaning method.

included_members.explanation: Uses gentle agitation/airflow to mechanically dislodge contaminants once adhesion is weakened.

included_members.description: Remove, separate and retain detached solid particles from the chamber atmosphere to prevent re-deposition and enable disposal or cleaning of collected material.
included_members.explanation: Focuses on capturing detached dry particles via filtration/separation to prevent re-deposition.

included_members.idea_text: A sealed garment cleaning chamber where clothes are suspended. An array of micro-jets or pulsators generates highly localized, tunable air pressure pulsations around individual fabric fibers. These rapid, non-linear air movements create micro-turbulences and pressure differentials that physically dislodge dry dirt, dust, and lint particles without harsh mechanical contact or significant bulk air movement. Dislodged particles are then quietly drawn into a filter system by a very gentle, continuous background flow.

included_members.description: An array of small, addressable actuation sources that generate rapid, tunable, non‑linear pressure pulses or vortical micro‑flows targeted at fabric fibers to create micro‑turbulence and pressure differentials that detach particles.

included_members.idea_text: Garments are treated with a dissolvable or detachable nanocoating that has a stronger affinity for dirt/oils than for fabric fibers. After wear, the garments are placed in a gentle tumbling drum or cabinet. A mild, fabric-safe trigger (e.g., a specific light wavelength, a slight humidity change, or a very mild vibration) causes the nanocoating to rapidly delaminate or de-bond from the fabric, encapsulating and releasing the accumulated dirt. The shed nanocoating and dirt particles are then collected by a vacuum and filter system, leaving clean fabric with no water.
included_members.abstraction: Localized vacuum/filtration capture and gentle handling: A mechanical system that collects the shed coating and entrained particles, separates them from the garments, and confines waste for disposal or recycling.
included_members.label: Localized vacuum/filtration capture and gentle handling
included_members.description: A mechanical system that collects the shed coating and entrained particles, separates them from the garments, and confines waste for disposal or recycling.
included_members.explanation: Uses vacuum/filtration to mechanically collect the detached coating and entrained soils without water.

included_members.idea_text: A specialized cleaning plate or drum lining made of a piezoelectric material. Clothes are gently pressed against or tumbled on this surface. Interdigitated electrodes on the surface generate high-frequency SAWs that propagate along the interface with the fabric. These SAWs exert precise, localized mechanical forces on dirt particles at the fabric surface, effectively "sweeping" or "vibrating" them off without needing bulk water, solvents, or bulk ultrasonic cavitation. The dislodged dirt is collected by an integrated vacuum system.
included_members.abstraction: Air-suction collection and separation: Remove and contain particles once detached by aspirating them away from the interface and separating solids from the airflow for disposal or filtering.
included_members.label: Air-suction collection and separation
included_members.description: Remove and contain particles once detached by aspirating them away from the interface and separating solids from the airflow for disposal or filtering.
included_members.explanation: Aspirates and separates detached particles via airflow/suction (dry particle extraction).
